newsitem.title: USA: Duke 846 MW Oconee, S.C. unit in startup.
newsitem.headline: Duke 846 MW Oconee, S.C. unit in startup.

text.p: Duke Power Co's 846 megawatt (MW) Oconee nuclear power unit 3 was in a startup mode as of early Monday following a shutdown which began in October, 1996, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said.

The unit, located in Seneca, S.C., was operating at 10 percent power as of early Monday but was "having problems with the new integrated control system (ICS)," the NRC said in its daily plant status report.
"We're doing some fine tuning to the ICS now," Duke spokesman Rick Zuercher said Monday, adding "we're still looking at returning the unit (to service) early this week."
The new ICS equipment was installed during the recent outage, the spokesman said.
Oconee 3 was taken off line for pipe inspections after a steam pipe burst at the adjacent unit 2, injuring seven workers.
Oconee units 1 and 2, each with a capacity of 846 MW, were operating at full power as of early Monday, the NRC said.
